question: How many pairs of gill slits are present in the members of class cyclostomata of phylum vertebrata?
solution:
The correct answer is **__6 - 15__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• "**Cyclostomata**" is a group that encompasses the two extant subclasses of **jawless fish **under the class Agnatha, namely hagfish and lampreys.
 
• Cyclostomes are a class of jawless vertebrates. They have an elongated body which bears **6-15 pairs of gill slits for respiration**.
 
• **Characteristics of Cyclostomata**
 
 
• The body is round and elongated, similar to an eel.
 
• Paired fins are absent.
 
• Median fins are present, with cartilaginous fin rays.
 
• There are no paired appendages.
 
• The skin is soft, smooth, and devoid of any scales.
 
• The spleen is not present.
 
• There is no exoskeleton.
 
• The endoskeleton is cartilaginous, with no bones.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Sub-Divisions of Cyclostomata**
 
• The cyclostomes are subdivided into two major orders.
 
• **Petromyzontiformes**
 
 
• This order includes lampreys and lamper eels.
 
• They can be found in both saltwater and freshwater.
 
• They have a ventral mouth that is filled with horny teeth.
 
• The nostril is located dorsally.
 
• Their dorsal fin is substantially developed.
 
• Spinal nerves have separate dorsal and ventral origins.
 
• The progression is indirect.
 
• For example, Petromyzon and Lampetra.
 
 
 
• **Myxiniformes**
 
 
• This order is represented by Myxiniformes Hagfishes.
 
• They are only found in the aquatic environment.
 
• They have a terminal mouth and only a few teeth.
 
• They do not have a buccal cavity.
 
• The nostril is the end of the tube.
 
• They have 6 to 14 pairs of gill slits.
 
• The spinal nerves' dorsal and ventral roots are not distinct.
 
• Eggs are big and in short supply.
 
• Dorsal fins are frequently absent or feeble.
